q: Do leaks from CO2 refrigeration systems count in Scope 1?
title: Leaks from CO2 (R744) systems
short: Yes, but they are tiny. CO2 as a refrigerant, called R744, has a global warming potential of 1, so a 10 kg leak is 10 kg CO2e. The same leak of a common HFC would count hundreds or thousands of times more. Record top-ups like any refrigerant.
audience: Cold stores, supermarkets and food plants

ul: Electricity use, which is usually far larger than leaks.
Any HFC used in a cascade system.
Top-up records from the service contractor.

p: Compare total emissions over the system life, electricity plus leaks, not only the refrigerant GWP.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
